title: Importance of Safety Training
content: Explain why ongoing safety training matters, not just a once-off induction. Cover: the OHS Act requires employers to inform, instruct and train employees on hazards specific to their work (section 13). Discuss how untrained workers are far more likely to be involved in incidents. Ask the team when they last had refresher training and on what.

title: Housekeeping and Worksite Cleanliness
content: Poor housekeeping causes slips, trips, falls, and fire hazards. Cover: keeping walkways clear, proper storage of tools and materials, immediate cleanup of spills, and correct waste disposal. A tidy site is a safer site - discuss what 'clean as you go' looks like on this job.

title: Proper Use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
content: PPE is the last line of defence, not the first. Cover: correct selection for the task, proper fit and inspection before use, when PPE must be replaced, and the employer's duty to provide it free of charge. Discuss any PPE issues the team has experienced (poor fit, damage, discomfort).

title: Slips, Trips, and Falls Prevention
content: The most common cause of workplace injury. Cover: uneven surfaces, trailing cables, wet floors, poor lighting, and inappropriate footwear. Walk the team through this site's specific trip hazards and how to report them.

title: Fire Safety and Extinguisher Use
content: Cover: the fire triangle (heat, fuel, oxygen), types of fire extinguishers and which fire class each is for, the PASS technique (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep), and this site's evacuation routes and assembly point. Confirm everyone knows where the nearest extinguisher is.

title: Electrical Safety Basics
content: Cover: never touching electrical equipment with wet hands, checking cables and plugs for damage before use, respecting isolation/lockout tags, and the danger of overloaded extension leads. Remind the team that electrical work is only for authorised, competent persons.

title: Hazard Communication (HazCom)
content: Cover: reading Safety Data Sheets (SDS) before using any chemical, understanding GHS pictograms and hazard labels, and knowing where the site's SDS file is kept. Ask the team to name a hazard symbol they've seen recently and what it means.

title: Emergency Evacuation Procedures
content: Cover: the alarm signal for this site, primary and secondary evacuation routes, the assembly point, and the role of fire marshals/wardens. Discuss what to do if a route is blocked, and confirm everyone knows who does headcounts.

title: First Aid and CPR Awareness
content: Cover: who the site's trained first aiders are and where the first aid box is located, the basics of primary response (check, call, care), and when to call emergency services rather than attempt treatment. Encourage anyone interested in first aid certification to speak to their supervisor.

title: Reporting Near Misses and Incidents
content: A near miss today can be tomorrow's serious injury if ignored. Cover: what counts as a reportable incident under the OHS Act (section 24), why near-miss reporting is protected and encouraged rather than punished, and how to submit a report on this site. Ask if anyone has had a close call recently that wasn't reported.

title: Hand Tool Safety
content: Cover: inspecting tools before use, using the right tool for the job, keeping cutting edges sharp and guarded, and safe storage to prevent damage or injury. Discuss any tools on site that are due for replacement.

title: Power Tool Safety
content: Cover: checking cords and guards before use, wearing appropriate PPE (eye/ear protection), keeping hands clear of moving parts, and never removing safety guards. Remind the team that only trained, authorised users should operate power tools.

title: Heavy Equipment Operation
content: Cover: pre-use inspection checklists, operator competency and certification requirements, exclusion zones around moving equipment, and the danger of blind spots. Discuss ground conditions and load limits relevant to this site.

title: Forklift Safety
content: Cover: pedestrian exclusion zones, load stability and rated capacity, the danger of overhead obstructions, and mandatory horn use at blind corners. Only certificated operators may drive - confirm who on site holds a valid licence.

title: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedures
content: Cover: isolating energy sources before maintenance, applying personal locks and tags, verifying zero energy state before starting work, and never removing another person's lock. This is one of the most safety-critical procedures on any site - walk through the steps for equipment relevant here.

title: Scaffolding Safety
content: Cover: scaffolds may only be erected, altered or dismantled by competent, appointed persons (Construction Regulations reg 16), weekly inspection tags, guardrails and toe-boards, and never overloading a platform. Confirm today's scaffold inspection tag is current.

title: Ladder Safety
content: Cover: the 4:1 angle rule, inspecting for damage before use, maintaining three points of contact, never standing on the top two rungs, and securing the ladder top and bottom. Remind the team ladders are for short-duration light work, not extended tasks.

title: Crane and Rigging Safety
content: Cover: only certificated riggers and signallers, checking sling and shackle condition and rated capacity before every lift, exclusion zones under suspended loads, and clear hand signals or radio communication. Discuss the load chart for equipment in use on this site.

title: Welding and Cutting Safety
content: Cover: fire watch requirements, removing combustibles from the work area, proper ventilation for fumes, eye and skin protection, and hot work permits. Discuss confined space precautions if welding will occur in an enclosed area.

title: Machine Guarding
content: Cover: never removing or bypassing a guard, reporting damaged or missing guards immediately, and the specific pinch points and rotating parts on machinery used here. Ask if anyone has seen a guard removed or propped open recently.

title: Working at Heights (Fall Protection)
content: Cover: the requirement for a documented fall protection plan for any work above 2m, harness inspection before use, anchor point suitability, and rescue planning. Confirm today's task has been assessed and the right fall protection is in place.

title: Confined Space Entry
content: Cover: atmospheric testing before and during entry, permit-to-work requirements, standby person and rescue arrangements, and never entering without authorisation. Discuss what qualifies as a confined space on this site and why entry without a permit is strictly forbidden.

title: Excavation and Trenching Safety
content: Cover: shoring or benching requirements for trenches over 1.5m deep, daily inspection before entry, safe access/egress points, and keeping spoil piles back from the edge. Discuss underground services checks done for this excavation.

title: Heat Stress Prevention
content: Cover: recognising early signs (cramps, heavy sweating, fatigue) versus heat stroke (confusion, dry skin, collapse), hydration schedules, shaded rest breaks, and acclimatisation for new workers. Discuss today's conditions and adjust the work-rest schedule if needed.

title: Cold Weather Safety
content: Cover: layering and appropriate clothing, recognising early hypothermia and frostbite signs, warm-up breaks, and the added risk of reduced dexterity when handling tools in the cold.

title: Noise Exposure and Hearing Protection
content: Cover: which areas or tasks on this site exceed the noise action level, correct fitting of ear plugs or muffs, and the cumulative, irreversible nature of hearing damage. Ask the team if hearing protection has been comfortable and effective.

title: Chemical Handling and Storage
content: Cover: reading labels and SDS before use, compatible storage (never mixing incompatible chemicals), spill response procedures, and correct PPE for the specific chemical in use. Point out where chemicals are stored on this site.

title: Asbestos Awareness
content: Cover: asbestos is only a risk when disturbed - never drill, cut, or sand suspected asbestos-containing material. Discuss how to recognise likely locations in older buildings and the legal requirement to stop and report suspected asbestos rather than continue work.

title: Lead Safety
content: Cover: exposure routes (inhalation of dust/fumes, ingestion), the importance of not eating or smoking in lead work areas, handwashing before breaks, and medical surveillance requirements for exposed workers.

title: Silica Dust Exposure
content: Cover: which tasks generate silica dust (cutting, grinding, drilling concrete/masonry), wet cutting methods to suppress dust, respiratory protection requirements, and the long-term lung disease risk of repeated exposure.

title: Defensive Driving
content: Cover: maintaining safe following distance, anticipating other road users' mistakes, adjusting speed for conditions, and the danger of fatigue on long drives. Discuss any recent near-misses on the road relevant to this team.

title: Backing Safety for Vehicles
content: Cover: using a spotter/banksman where visibility is limited, checking mirrors and blind spots before reversing, and sounding the horn before moving. Discuss reversing hazards specific to this site's layout.

title: Seat Belt Use in Work Vehicles
content: Cover: seat belts are mandatory in all site and company vehicles regardless of distance or speed, and their role in preventing ejection during a collision or rollover. No exceptions, no excuses.

title: Pedestrian Safety on Job Sites
content: Cover: designated walkways separate from vehicle routes, high-visibility clothing requirements, eye contact with drivers/operators before crossing, and never walking behind reversing equipment.

title: Distracted Driving Prevention
content: Cover: the danger of phone use while driving (even hands-free), eating, or adjusting equipment while moving. Discuss the company's policy on phone use in vehicles and encourage pulling over for calls.

title: Proper Lifting Techniques
content: Cover: bending at the knees not the back, keeping the load close to the body, avoiding twisting while lifting, and asking for help or using mechanical aids for heavy/awkward loads. Demonstrate correct technique if practical.

title: Repetitive Motion Injury Prevention
content: Cover: recognising early signs of strain (tingling, numbness, aching), the value of micro-breaks and task rotation, and adjusting workstation or tool grip to reduce strain. Ask if anyone is experiencing discomfort from repetitive tasks.

title: Workplace Ergonomics
content: Cover: correct seating and screen height for desk-based work, adjusting workstations to the individual rather than the individual adjusting to the workstation, and the cumulative cost of poor posture over time.

title: Hydration and Health on the Job
content: Cover: the link between dehydration and reduced concentration/increased accident risk, especially in hot conditions, and encouraging regular water intake throughout the shift rather than only at breaks.

title: Fatigue Management
content: Cover: recognising the signs of fatigue in yourself and colleagues, the increased accident risk of long shifts or poor sleep, and the importance of speaking up if you're too tired to work safely. No task is worth pushing through dangerous fatigue.

title: Working Near Water Safety
content: Cover: life jacket requirements near open water, rescue equipment availability, and the added risk of slippery surfaces near water bodies. Discuss specific water hazards on this site.

title: Lightning Safety Outdoors
content: Cover: the 30-30 rule (seek shelter if thunder follows lightning within 30 seconds, wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before resuming), and which equipment/activities must stop immediately when lightning is detected on this site.

title: Wildlife and Insect Hazards
content: Cover: awareness of snakes, spiders, bees/wasps and other local hazards relevant to this site's location, what to do if bitten or stung, and never approaching or provoking wildlife encountered on site.

title: Radiation Safety
content: Only relevant where radiography, radioactive sources, or similar equipment are in use on this site. Cover: exclusion zones during use, dosimeter requirements for exposed workers, and strict adherence to the site's radiation safety officer's instructions.

title: Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) Safety
content: Relevant in wastewater, petrochemical, and some mining/agricultural settings. Cover: H2S is colourless and its 'rotten egg' smell disappears at dangerous concentrations (odour fatigue), the need for gas detectors in at-risk areas, and immediate evacuation on alarm.

title: Drug and Alcohol Awareness
content: Cover: the OHS Act General Safety Regulations prohibit working under the influence, the danger impaired judgement poses to the whole team, and the confidential support available to anyone struggling with substance use. This is about safety, not punishment.

title: Workplace Violence Prevention
content: Cover: recognising escalating conflict early, de-escalation basics, the reporting process for threats or aggressive behaviour, and the company's zero-tolerance stance on workplace violence.

title: Stress Management
content: Cover: recognising stress in yourself and colleagues, healthy coping strategies, the impact of chronic stress on concentration and safety, and where to find support if work or personal stress is becoming overwhelming.

title: Mental Health Awareness
content: Cover: reducing stigma around mental health conversations at work, recognising when a colleague may be struggling, and how to point someone toward support resources. A safe site looks after minds as well as bodies.

title: Team Communication for Safety
content: Cover: speaking up when you see an unsafe act, the buddy system for high-risk tasks, clear handover communication between shifts, and creating a culture where raising concerns is welcomed, not punished.
